properties.name: UNMEASURED, and it is now a live risk: the payload-in-the-text-block shape doubles WIRE BYTES, and nobody has checked whether any client injects BOTH representations and doubles the model's tokens too
properties.statement:
FLO2 F26 raises it and explicitly declines to assume it away: "⚠️ The doubling is WIRE BYTES, not necessarily MODEL TOKENS. A client picks one representation to put in front of the model; it does not normally inject both. So the cost lands on a local pipe or an HTTP body, not on the context budget — which is the budget reflow2 actually guards with `budget_chars`. That said, a client that injects both WOULD double the tokens, and nobody has checked whether any does. Worth measuring before assuming it away."

⭐ IT STOPPED BEING HYPOTHETICAL ON 2026-09-21. The reply-shape FALLBACK moved from `signpost` to `duplicate` (`chg:an-unmeasured-client-gets-the-payload-not-a-signpost`), so every client not on the measured list — which is every connector, by construction — now receives the payload in `content` AND in `structuredContent`. If any of them concatenates both into the model's context, that client's context cost for a reflow2 reply doubled on that change, silently.

WHAT IS KNOWN, AND IT IS NOT THIS. Two clients have been measured for WHICH field they read: Grok Build keeps only the text block and stores no copy of `structuredContent`; OpenCode hands its model only the text block and fills it from `structuredContent` only when empty. Both are single-representation readers, so for both the change is free. NOTHING has been measured about Claude's connector, ChatGPT's, or any other — and those are precisely the population the fallback now serves.

WHY IT WAS ACCEPTED ANYWAY, so this is not read as an oversight: the alternative default was the signpost, which flo2 measured as failing BOTH populations outright. A possible doubling for an unknown subset is a smaller and more recoverable harm than a certain failure for all of them, and `reply_budget` caps a JSON reply at 30,000 characters so the worst case is bounded. The trade was taken knowingly.

HOW IT WOULD BE MEASURED: point one connector at a server, call one structured tool, and read what the client actually put in the model's context — the same method that answered the question for Grok Build (its session store) and OpenCode (its source). Until then this is an open exposure, not a defect, and the honest statement is that nobody has looked.
